page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-48GB is a Cloud Native server configured with 8 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes KVM virtualization and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. Single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores align with the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth presents a similar contrast: small-block cached read operations perform at an average level of 830.42 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the bottom 25% weak category.

Given the shared CPU allocation and average multi-core capabilities, this server is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations, which perform in the average tier. It is less suitable for memory-intensive large-block operations or complex LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model drop to a poor 6.18 tokens/sec. The shared resource model offers a cost-efficient entry point for multi-threaded applications that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core execution.
